title: A simple method of human sperm vitrification
author: Shah, Rasappan, et al.

steps.title: Collect and analyze semen sample
steps.instruction: Obtain semen by masturbation after 3–5 days of abstinence, obtain written informed consent, and perform routine WHO 2010 semen analysis. Use the leftover sample for vitrification.

steps.title: Swim‑up sperm selection (optional for low motility)
steps.instruction: Overlay 0.5 mL standard gamete‑handling medium (supplemented with 10 mg/mL human serum albumin, Quinn’s Advantage, REF ART‑1023, Cooper Surgical, Denmark) onto 1 mL semen in a tube. Incubate 45 min at room temperature. Aspirate the top 0.4 mL motile fraction, leaving the interface.

steps.title: Adjust sperm concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the aspirated motile fraction with the same medium to reach a final concentration of 10 × 10⁶ sperm/mL.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 M sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 mol sucrose in 1 L molecular‑grade double‑distilled (Millipore‑treated) water to make a fresh 0.5 M sucrose solution.

steps.title: Mix sperm with sucrose (1:1)
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of the freshly prepared 0.5 M sucrose solution to the sperm suspension drop‑by‑drop with gentle agitation (1 part sperm + 1 part sucrose) to obtain a final sperm concentration of 5 × 10⁶ sperm/mL.

steps.title: Set up vitrification apparatus
steps.instruction: Place a stainless‑steel tea strainer inside liquid nitrogen. Pre‑cool cryovials in liquid nitrogen for later storage.

steps.title: Vitrify sperm droplets
steps.instruction: Using a micropipette, dispense 30 µL of the sperm‑sucrose mixture as a droplet held 20–30 cm above the liquid nitrogen surface inside a thermocol box; the droplet contacts liquid nitrogen, instantly forming a solid sphere that settles to the bottom of the tea strainer.

steps.title: Transfer spheres to cryovials
steps.instruction: Immediately after sphere formation, transfer the spheres from the tea strainer into pre‑cooled cryovials and store them in liquid nitrogen (minimum 1 week storage).

steps.title: Warm (devitrify) sperm spheres
steps.instruction: Remove cryovials after storage, and submerge the spheres in 5 mL pre‑warmed gamete‑handling medium (supplemented with human serum albumin) at 42 °C for exactly 10 seconds.

steps.title: Assess post‑warm sperm quality
steps.instruction: Immediately evaluate sperm motility and viability under a light microscope at 400× magnification.

steps.title: Optional: Large‑volume handling
steps.instruction: If the semen volume exceeds 4 mL, divide it into two 2 mL aliquots, perform swim‑up on each (as above) because a single Nunc cryotube holds only 2 mL. Transfer spheres rapidly to cryovials to avoid spontaneous thawing.
